title: Member Services Training Notes: Credit Balance Carried Into the Latest Payment Arrangements Bill at a Default
content:
**Member services training — Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements): a credit balance carried into the latest bill**

**The rule.** A credit balance carried into the latest bill is applied at a default according to the recent returns on the member's Electric Service by Rate Schedule account: in full where no returned payment was posted in the three months ending on the default date, at 50 percent (0.5) of it where one was, and not at all where no credit balance was carried.

**What a carried credit balance is.** The credit balance carried into the latest bill is the service account's balance less that bill's charges and plus its credits, where that result is below zero; the credit balance is the amount by which it is below zero. *That bill* is the bill of the latest installment's billing period; *its charges* are the usage lines, service fees, late payment charges and program charges billed for that billing period; *its credits* are the bill credits posted for that billing period.

**Questions answered in training**

*How is the carried credit balance found on a hypothetical account?* Balance $40.00, latest bill charges $130.00, latest bill credits $15.00: $40.00 less $130.00 plus $15.00 is $75.00 below zero, so the credit balance carried into the latest bill is $75.00.

*And when the same reckoning comes out at or above zero?* No credit balance was carried, and nothing is applied under this rule.

*How much of the $75.00 is applied?* $75.00 where no returned payment was posted in the three months ending on the default date; $37.50 where one was.

| Credit balance carried into the latest bill | Returned payment in the 3 months ending on the default date | Applied |
|---|---|---|
| yes | no | in full |
| yes | yes | 50 percent |
| no | — | nothing |
